clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old female presented with progressive dyspnea, initially suspected to be pulmonary embolism. A Chest CT scan revealed a large (70 mm × 75 mm × 105 mm) heterogeneously enhancing solid mass in the left kidney with tumor thrombosis extending into the left renal vein and IVC, causing pulmonary thromboembolism. A 7 mm ground-glass nodule was also noted in the left lower lobe. Following left radical nephrectomy, macroscopic examination showed a 7 cm × 6.5 cm × 5 cm mass. Microscopic examination revealed sheet-like diffuse infiltration of small, round neoplastic cells with monomorphic nuclei, fine speckled chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and occasional pseudorosette-like structures. Immunohistochemistry showed dot-like staining with CK AE1/AE3, positive nuclear reaction with NKX2.2, diffuse membranous staining with CD99, and negative staining with TLE1. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) identified an EWSR1 gene rearrangement (translocation at 11;22), confirming the diagnosis of peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET/Ewing sarcoma). Anticoagulant therapy was initiated and continued due to prothrombotic risk. Systemic chemotherapy was initiated 2 months postoperatively.

Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) study identified translocation at (11;22), indicating the presence of an EWSR1 gene rearrangement, confirming PNET/Ewing sarcoma.
Anticoagulant therapy was initiated and continued due to prothrombotic risk associated with malignancy and chemotherapy.
Systemic chemotherapy was initiated 2 months postoperatively as part of her comprehensive treatment plan.
